Agent skill bundles: portable folders with instructions, scripts and resources loaded on demand by the coding agent (Agent Skills standard); SkillMOO evolves a task-specific subset/edited version of the bundle; optimizer skill for the optimizer agent; Pareto archive of candidate bundles

fields.v: Tasks: all 16 SE tasks of SkillsBench. Configurations: SkillMOO, ori_skill, no_skill. Baseline: no_skill (and ori_skill as static practice). Held constant: model GLM-5 for solver and optimizer, task, expanded tests applied uniformly, 900 s timeout. Acceptance tests: expanded suites of 40-43 tests (GPT-5.4-generated, manually checked, original compile/build gates retained). Repetitions: 10 runs per method per task. Human intervention: none stated

SkillMOO best pass rate rank on 11 of 12 non-zero-pass tasks; avg pass 0.39 vs 0.14 (ori_skill) vs 0.21 (no_skill); avg cost 0.71 vs 0.89 vs 0.64. Best case task 5: pass 0.16 -> 0.37 (+21.3 pp), cost -32.1%, runtime -23.6% vs ori_skill (Scott-Knott ESD significant). Claimed gains up to +42 pp and cost reductions up to 32.1%. no_skill cheapest (rank 1 cost on 12 of 16; on four tasks not statistically distinct). HV improved on all 12 tasks; break-even 5-682 reuses (median 45). Edits: Remove (16) and Replace (7) associated with pass gains; Add 0/9. Significance: Scott-Knott ESD ranks

Distinguished configurations on pass and cost on most tasks; 4 tasks gave zero pass for all methods (container memory/build-time limits) and were excluded. Repeatable: 10 runs with SD reported; replication package. Limitations stated: single benchmark; 1-8 initial skills; LLM-generated tests from the same model family (GPT-5.4 vs GLM-5 is said to be 'same model family'); one LLM; edit analysis exploratory, not causal

Single benchmark and small skill pools; one LLM (transfer to GPT or Claude open); test expansion bias; edit patterns descriptive. Agenda: causal evaluation of skill edits, cost-aware skill routing and reuse, cross-task and cross-model transfer, continuous skill maintenance
